frequency_question: How often do major bipartisan energy permitting reform bills pass into law in the US Congress during a divided government context within a 2-year window?
membership_rule: Includes major omnibus bills or targeted permitting packages attempting to reform NEPA/interstate pipelines with bipartisan backing; excludes minor appropriations riders or single-agency administrative fixes.
provenance_note: claimed 1 hits but 2 of 3 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 3 named major episodes capturing the structural dynamics of modern permitting reform attempts
known_gaps: Minor procedural reform riders attached to must-pass NDAAs or continuing resolutions are excluded but affect the margin.
skeleton: 3 distinct legislative pushes under divided or narrow-majority control over 3 decades
multiplier: 1 hit for comprehensive energy (2005), 1 partial hit via debt ceiling deal (2023), 1 complete miss for standalone permitting (2022)
validity_reason: Base rate tied to congressional polarization dynamics and committee jurisdictions which remain stable through the current congressional cycle.
